advances: A direct extension of a Guedon-Milman-form isotropic lower-tail estimate to complete discrete log-affine laws with integral means is false, even after imposing arbitrarily large entropy above the dyadic scale and arbitrarily small normalized atomic contributions. The obstruction is that rare outer lattice columns supply half the covariance trace, although almost every sample lies in the middle columns. The same original mean rows have uniformly positive actual closed-halfspace depth at their means. This attacks that particular continuous-to-lattice transfer, not other possible bridges, an actual third-moment bound, or the locked Weak Oertel conjecture.
author: research-agent
proof:
The triangle's only integral first-coordinate columns are
\[
D_M=\{(0,y):0\le y\le M\}
\cup\{(1,y):0\le y\le M/2\}
\cup\{(2,0)\},
\]
where all vertical coordinates are integers. Indeed, its inequalities are \(x\ge0\), \(y\ge0\), and \(x/2+y/M\le1\). Its vertices belong to \(D_M\), so \(\operatorname{conv}(D_M)=P_M\). The convex hull of a Cartesian product of finite sets is the product of their convex hulls: one inclusion follows by projecting a convex combination, and the other follows by multiplying convex-combination coefficients in the factors. Thus \(\operatorname{conv}(D)=P_M^b\), and intersecting with \(\mathbb Z^{2b}\) gives \(D_M^b=D\). The triangle is two-dimensional, so the product has dimension \(N\). Since \(4\mid M\), the point \(\mathbf j_M\) is integral; its coordinates are positive and \(1/2+(M/4)/M=3/4<1\), so the product mean root is interior.

The law of the third construction in `1ed6b6d9eb994c90` assigns unnormalized weight \(1\) to each point of the first column, \(s\) to each point of the middle column, and \(s^2=M+1\) to the apex. The first column therefore has total weight \(M+1\), equal to the apex weight. Summing all three columns gives the stated \(Z\). Thus \(X\) takes values \(0,1,2\) with probabilities \(\alpha,1-2\alpha,\alpha\). Conditional on these values, \(Y\) is respectively uniform on \(\{0,\ldots,M\}\), uniform on \(\{0,\ldots,M/2\}\), and zero. In particular \(\mathbb EX=1\) and
\(\mathbb EY=\alpha M/2+(1-2\alpha)M/4=M/4\), independently confirming the exact mean. The product table is
\(p_{\mathbf x}=Z^{-b}\exp((\log s)\sum_{i=1}^b x_i)\)
for \(\mathbf x=((x_1,y_1),\ldots,(x_b,y_b))\in D\). This proves positivity and global log-affinity on the complete support, with product tilt \(((\log s,0),\ldots,(\log s,0))\).

To check the product entropy-row identification directly, let \(q\) be any law on \(D\) with mean \(\mathbf j\). Affinity of \(\log p\) gives \(\sum q_{\mathbf x}\log p_{\mathbf x}=b\log s-b\log Z\), the same value as under \(p\). Therefore \(D(q\|p)=H(p)-H(q)\). The inequality \(u\log u\ge u-1\), with its continuous value at zero, implies \(D(q\|p)\ge0\), with equality only when \(q=p\). Thus \(p\) is indeed the unique maximum-entropy row at the original mean, agreeing with the block rows in `1ed6b6d9eb994c90` and the product-row alias in `af3581e517f3a94e`.

Since \(Z>2(M+1)\), one has \(0<\alpha<1/2\). Dividing its numerator and denominator by \(s\) gives \(\alpha=s/(2s+M/2+1)\le2s/M\). The inequalities \(s^2=M+1\le2M\) and \(2\sqrt2<3\) imply \(\alpha\le3/\sqrt M=3/(2b^2)\).

The conditional mean of \(V\) is zero in every column: its three values of \(\mathbb E[V\mid X]\) are \(M/2-M/2\), \(M/4+M/4-M/2\), and \(0+M/2-M/2\). Thus \(\mathbb EV=0\) and \(\mathbb E[UV]=\mathbb E[U\mathbb E(V\mid X)]=0\). Also \(U\) takes values \(-1,0,1\) with the above probabilities, so its variance is \(2\alpha\).

For a uniform integer \(Y_L\) on \(\{0,\ldots,L\}\), the sums of the first and second powers give \(\mathbb EY_L=L/2\) and \(\mathbb EY_L^2=L(2L+1)/6\); hence \(\operatorname{Var}Y_L=L(L+2)/12\). The conditional variances of \(V\) are consequently \(M(M+2)/12\), \(M(M+4)/48\), and zero. All its conditional means vanish, so
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Var}_\nu V
&=\alpha\frac{M(M+2)}{12}
 +(1-2\alpha)\frac{M(M+4)}{48}\\
&=\frac{M[(1+2\alpha)M+4]}{48}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Both variances are strictly positive. The displayed map defining \(\Xi\) has, on a block centered at \((1,M/4)\), linear matrix
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
(2\alpha)^{-1/2}&0\\
(M/4)(\operatorname{Var}_\nu V)^{-1/2}&
(\operatorname{Var}_\nu V)^{-1/2}
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
It is invertible. Its two output coordinates have unit variances and zero covariance; distinct blocks remain independent. This proves \(\mathbb E\Xi=0\) and \(\operatorname{Cov}(\Xi)=I_N\). An invertible covariance-whitening matrix has Gram matrix equal to the inverse source covariance, by rearranging its covariance identity. Consequently \(\|\Xi\|^2=(\mathbf X-\mathbf j)^\top\operatorname{Cov}_p(\mathbf X)^{-1}(\mathbf X-\mathbf j)\), which is also the squared norm for the symmetric covariance inverse square root. Thus the norm counterexample does not depend on choosing this particular whitening. Invertibility also proves that the support and all atom probabilities are merely transported, not replaced. Finite support makes the transported probability singular with respect to Lebesgue measure.

On a middle column, \(U=0\) and \(V=Y-M/4\) with \(0\le Y\le M/2\). Consequently
\[
0\le\frac{V^2}{\operatorname{Var}_\nu V}
\le\frac{3M}{(1+2\alpha)M+4}\le3,\qquad
\mathbb E\!\left[\frac{V^2}{\operatorname{Var}_\nu V}\,\middle|\,X=1\right]
=\frac{M+4}{(1+2\alpha)M+4}\le1.
\]
Let \(E\) be the event that all \(b\) blocks are in their middle columns. Product structure gives \(\Pr_p(E)=(1-2\alpha)^b\), and the union bound gives \(\Pr_p(E^c)\le2b\alpha\). Conditional on \(E\), the middle-column vertical coordinates remain independent. Each squared normalized vertical coordinate lies in \([0,3]\) and has expectation at most one, so its variance is at most its second moment, which is at most three times its expectation and hence at most three. Therefore
\[
\mathbb E_p[\|\Xi\|^2\mid E]\le b,\qquad
\operatorname{Var}_p(\|\Xi\|^2\mid E)\le3b.
\]
Chebyshev's inequality gives \(\Pr_p(\|\Xi\|^2>3b/2\mid E)\le12/b\), since the threshold exceeds the conditional mean by at least \(b/2\). It follows, without multiplying possibly negative lower bounds, that
\[
\Pr_p(\|\Xi\|^2>3b/2)
\le\Pr_p(E^c)+\Pr_p(\|\Xi\|^2>3b/2\mid E)
\le2b\alpha+12/b\le15/b.
\]
For small \(b\) the resulting negative lower bound is automatic, and for \(b\to\infty\) it proves the stated limit. The identity \((1-t_0)^2N=(3/4)(2b)=3b/2\) gives the asserted norm threshold. Each horizontal normalized coordinate still has variance one, although all of them vanish on \(E\), whose probability tends to one. This verifies the rare-column covariance mechanism exactly.

Since \(s>1\), the largest block atom is the apex, of probability \(s^2/Z=\alpha\). Independence proves \(p_{\max}=\alpha^b\), and \(2^N=4^b\) proves the formula and bound for \(\rho\). Also
\[
\sum_{\mathbf x\in D}p_{\mathbf x}^4
\le p_{\max}^3\sum_{\mathbf x\in D}p_{\mathbf x}
=p_{\max}^3,
\]
so multiplying by \(8^N=(2^N)^3\) gives the normalized atomic bound. The estimate \((6/b^2)^b\to0\) follows by taking logarithms, since \(b(\log6-2\log b)\to-\infty\).

The original product tilt and original mean give
\(H(p)=b\log Z-(\log s)\sum_i\mathbb EX_i=b\log(Z/s)\).
Since \(Z/s=2s+M/2+1\ge M/2\),
\[
H(p)-N\log2\ge b\log(M/8)
=4b\log b-b\log2\longrightarrow+\infty.
\]
For any fixed \(A,c>0\), the proposed upper bound at \(t_0\) tends to zero as \(N=2b\to\infty\), whereas the lower-tail probability tends to one. The entropy and both atomic restrictions hold for all sufficiently large \(b\). Choosing \(b\) beyond these thresholds and beyond \(b_0\) proves the full quantified violation.

Finally apply `af3581e517f3a94e` with exactly the product-row alias stated above. Its hypotheses allow arbitrary even heights, arbitrary factor counts, and arbitrary supported roots; our heights are divisible by four and our roots are the supported \(\mathbf j_M\). Its conclusion therefore gives \(p(H)\ge\delta_\triangle\) for every closed halfspace containing \(\mathbf j\), establishing \(\tau_p(\mathbf j)\ge\delta_\triangle\). If one expresses these mean caps in the isotropic coordinates, the inverse affine image of a proper closed halfspace containing zero is a proper closed halfspace containing the same original \(\mathbf j\), so its probability has the same bound. This uses no new source or root law.

For every original root \(\mathbf a\in D\), a containing closed halfspace contains its atom, so \(\tau_p(\mathbf a)\ge p_{\mathbf a}\). Thus \(\mathcal M_3(p)\ge\sum p_{\mathbf a}^4\). An upper bound tending to zero for this atomic lower bound gives no upper bound on \(\mathcal M_3(p)\). Likewise, the norm estimate and its failure use no convex body or mixed-integer set from the locked problem. The proved obstruction is precisely the proposed discrete isotropic lower-tail inequality, with the uniformly positive actual mean-cap contrast retained.
statement:
All logarithms are natural. For each integer \(b\ge1\), set \(M=4b^4\), \(s=\sqrt{M+1}\), and \(N=2b\). Use exactly the third triangle, support, and integral row center of accepted fact `1ed6b6d9eb994c90`:
\[
P_M=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0),(0,M),(2,0)\},\qquad
D_M=P_M\cap\mathbb Z^2,\qquad
\mathbf j_M=(1,M/4).
\]
Let \(\nu\) be that fact's full-positive mean-\(\mathbf j_M\) entropy row, with tilt \((\log s,0)\) and normalizer \(Z=2(M+1)+(M/2+1)s\). Define the original support \(D=D_M^b\), original source law \(p=\nu^{\otimes b}\), and original mean root \(\mathbf j=(\mathbf j_M,\ldots,\mathbf j_M)\). Thus \(p\) is exactly \(Q_{\mathbf j}\) of accepted fact `af3581e517f3a94e`, with its factor count \(k=b\), all heights equal to \(M\), and all roots equal to \(\mathbf j_M\). Here \(b\) counts blocks, not the middle-layer cardinality in the second construction of `1ed6b6d9eb994c90`.

The support is full-dimensional and complete: \(\operatorname{conv}(D)=P_M^b\) and \(D=\operatorname{conv}(D)\cap\mathbb Z^N\). The original \(p\) is a positive globally log-affine table on all of \(D\), is its unique maximum-entropy mean-\(\mathbf j\) row, and has an integral interior mean \(\mathbf j\). Put
\[
\alpha=\frac{M+1}{2(M+1)+(M/2+1)s}.
\]
This \(\alpha\) is each outer-column probability and is exactly \(\pi_0\) in the interior-row description of `af3581e517f3a94e` for the present zero vertical tilt. It is not a new source tilt or an entropy reweighting. One has \(0<\alpha<1/2\) and \(\alpha\le3/\sqrt M\).

For one original block \((X,Y)\sim\nu\), define the centered linear coordinates \(U=X-1\) and \(V=Y+(M/4)X-M/2\). Then
\[
\mathbb E_\nu U=\mathbb E_\nu V=0,\qquad
\operatorname{Cov}_\nu(U,V)=0,\qquad
\operatorname{Var}_\nu U=2\alpha,\qquad
\operatorname{Var}_\nu V=\frac{M[(1+2\alpha)M+4]}{48}.
\]
For \(\mathbf X=((X_1,Y_1),\ldots,(X_b,Y_b))\sim p\), let
\[
\Xi=\left(
\frac{X_i-1}{\sqrt{2\alpha}},\,
\frac{Y_i+(M/4)X_i-M/2}{\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}_\nu V}}
\right)_{i=1}^b.
\]
This is only an invertible affine isotropic pushforward of the same \(\mathbf X\) and original root \(\mathbf j\): it has mean zero and covariance \(I_N\). Its support is the corresponding affine image of \(D\), and its law is a discrete probability measure, not a Lebesgue density. Neither \(\Xi\) nor its zero mean replaces the original table \(p\) or root \(\mathbf j\) in the depth or moment definitions below.

With the fixed number \(t_0=1-\sqrt3/2\in(0,1)\), this family satisfies
\[
\Pr_p\!\left(\|\Xi\|\le(1-t_0)\sqrt N\right)
=\Pr_p\!\left(\|\Xi\|^2\le\frac32 b\right)
\ge1-2b\alpha-\frac{12}{b}
\ge1-\frac{15}{b}
\longrightarrow1.
\]
Writing \(p_{\max}=\max_{\mathbf x\in D}p_{\mathbf x}\), \(\rho=2^N p_{\max}\), and \(H(p)=-\sum_{\mathbf x\in D}p_{\mathbf x}\log p_{\mathbf x}\), one also has
\[
\begin{aligned}
p_{\max}&=\alpha^b,\qquad
\rho=(4\alpha)^b\le(6/b^2)^b\longrightarrow0,\\
8^N\sum_{\mathbf x\in D}p_{\mathbf x}^4&\le\rho^3\longrightarrow0,\\
H(p)&=b\log\bigl(2s+M/2+1\bigr)\ge b\log(M/2),\\
H(p)-N\log2&\longrightarrow+\infty.
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, for every \(A,c,L,\varepsilon>0\) and every integer \(b_0\ge1\), some \(b\ge b_0\) in this family simultaneously satisfies \(H(p)-N\log2\ge L\), \(\rho\le\varepsilon\), \(8^N\sum p_{\mathbf x}^4\le\varepsilon\), and
\[
\Pr_p\!\left(\|\Xi\|\le(1-t_0)\sqrt N\right)
>A\exp\bigl(-c\sqrt N\,t_0^3\bigr).
\]
In particular no universal \(A,c>0\) make
\[
\Pr_p\!\left(\|\Xi\|\le(1-t)\sqrt N\right)
\le A\exp\bigl(-c\sqrt N\,t^3\bigr)
\]
valid for all complete full-dimensional integer supports, all positive globally log-affine laws with integral means in their supports, and all \(t\in(0,1)\), when \(\Xi\) denotes an affine covariance-whitening of the original source vector about its mean. This remains false after any fixed restrictions of the stated entropy and atomic types.

For the positive cap contrast, use actual closed-halfspace depth and the actual third moment under the original source law:
\[
\tau_p(\mathbf a)
:=\inf_{\substack{H\subseteq\mathbb R^N\text{ a proper closed halfspace}\\
\mathbf a\in H}}p(H),\qquad
\mathcal M_3(p):=\sum_{\mathbf a\in D}p_{\mathbf a}\tau_p(\mathbf a)^3.
\]
Every root weight in \(\mathcal M_3(p)\) is the original \(p_{\mathbf a}\); no mean-\(\mathbf a\) entropy row is substituted. With exactly the constants of `af3581e517f3a94e`,
\[
\kappa_\triangle=\max\{20288,144e^8,2982528\},\qquad
\delta_\triangle=\frac1{8\kappa_\triangle}>0,
\]
every closed halfspace containing the original mean \(\mathbf j\) has \(p\)-mass at least \(\delta_\triangle\), and hence \(\tau_p(\mathbf j)\ge\delta_\triangle\) for every \(b\). The quantity \(\sum p_{\mathbf x}^4\) above is only the atomic lower bound on \(\mathcal M_3(p)\), not \(\mathcal M_3(p)\) itself. No vanishing normalized actual third moment, and no mixed-integer body witnessing failure of the locked conjecture, is asserted.
